# Claims

1. A pipe clamp, comprising: a base having a saddle groove configured to receive a pipe; a cap having a cap groove facing the saddle groove, a first side of the cap being pivotally connected to a first side of the base; a spring arranged between the base and the cap and biasing the cap away from the base toward an open position; and a latch at a second side of the base, the latch being releasable and configured to hold the cap in a closed position against the spring.

2. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the spring is a compression spring seated in a pocket of the base.

3. The pipe clamp of claim 2, wherein the pocket is located beside the saddle groove at the second side of the base.

4. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the latch comprises a latch lug on the second side of the base, a cap latch lug on a second side of the cap, and a locking pin removably insertable through the latch lug and the cap latch lug when the cap is in the closed position, the latch lug has a hole receiving the locking pin, and the locking pin has a head at one end with a diameter larger than the hole.

5. The pipe clamp of claim 1, further comprising a hinge pin extending through a hinge lug on the first side of the base and a cap hinge lug on the first side of the cap, the cap pivoting on the hinge pin.

6. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the base comprises a base plate having mounting holes and a saddle block on the base plate, the saddle groove is a half-round groove in a top of the saddle block, and the base plate and the saddle block are one machined part.

7. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the base and the cap are made of glass-filled nylon.

8. A method of securing a pipe in a clamp, the clamp comprising a base having a saddle groove, a cap pivotally connected to the base by a hinge pin, and a spring biasing the cap away from the base, the method comprising, in the following order: placing the pipe in the saddle groove; pivoting the cap about the hinge pin onto the pipe; compressing the spring with the cap; pushing a locking pin through a latch lug of the base and a cap latch lug of the cap; and releasing the cap, the locking pin holding the cap closed against the spring.

9. The method of claim 8, further comprising, before placing the pipe in the saddle groove, fastening the base to a wall with screws through mounting holes of the base.

10. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulling the locking pin out of the latch lug and the cap latch lug, the spring then lifting the cap away from the pipe.
